claims: Discrete action shadow charge is algebraically equivalent, up to an action-independent constant, to full Bellman-Q action selection.
The shadow-charge policy is bit-identical to the exact online Bellman optimum given the exact belief, verified with zero mismatches.
Exact-belief shadow-charge pricing recovers the full economic gap over frozen pacing in the belief-sensitive environment (regret 0.000 vs recoverable gap 0.371).
The belief-estimation task is genuinely learnable: ridge regression recovers exactly zero regret, tied with the exact-belief oracle.
A genuinely trained FabricPC model recovers belief information above a naive baseline, under both predictive-coding and backprop training.
FabricPC's predictive-coding and same-topology-backprop training are statistically indistinguishable from each other under the tested bounded design.
FabricPC's belief-prediction MSE is approximately 600x worse than ridge's on the same declared features, and FabricPC captures only 15.4% of the recoverable regret gap.
nonclaims: FabricPC did not improve Compitum's production routing; no production code path was changed.
This work does not claim predictive coding is generally inferior to backpropagation -- only that the two tied under one small, fixed, bounded-training topology.

This work does not claim the belief-sensitive environment or shadow-charge mechanism is unsuitable for further research -- the opposite is demonstrated for the economic mechanism and task learnability.
This work does not justify or recommend any change to production constraints.shadow_prices or SwitchCertificate.
Whether a larger or differently configured FabricPC topology would close the measured gap with ridge was not investigated and is not claimed either way.
